theme: Military and civil officers; David’s final assembly
readingInstruction: Read 1 Chronicles 27:1-29:30. David organizes the kingdom, charges Solomon and the people, and gives toward the temple from his own treasure. Then he prays one of the great prayers of the Bible. Read 29:10-20 slowly.
settingTheScene: This is the end of 1 Chronicles. David is old, and the transition to Solomon is a formal public event. After listing the officers of the kingdom, the Chronicler records David’s final address to the assembly. He gives the plans for the temple to Solomon, urges the leaders to give, and then leads the people in blessing God. Solomon is made king a second time, and David dies “in a good old age, full of days, riches, and honor.”
observation: “Now therefore in the sight of all Israel, the assembly of the LORD, and in the hearing of our God, observe and seek out all the commandments of the LORD your God” (28:8).
“And you, Solomon my son, know the God of your father and serve him with a whole heart and with a willing mind” (28:9).
“If you seek him, he will be found by you, but if you forsake him, he will cast you off forever” (28:9).
“Be strong and courageous and do it. Do not be afraid and do not be dismayed, for the LORD God, even my God, is with you” (28:20).
“Who then is willing to offer willingly, consecrating himself today to the LORD?” (29:5).
“Then the people rejoiced because they had given willingly, for with a whole heart they had offered freely to the LORD” (29:9).
“Yours, O LORD, is the greatness and the power and the glory and the victory and the majesty” (29:11).
“For all things come from you, and of your own have we given you” (29:14).
interpretation:
David’s charge to Solomon is among the finest pieces of fatherly advice in Scripture. “Know the God of your father and serve him with a whole heart and with a willing mind.” Knowledge comes first, then service. The heart must be whole, undivided, and the mind willing. Then the sober promise: “If you seek him, he will be found by you, but if you forsake him, he will cast you off forever.” This is the Chronicler’s whole theology in one verse. Seek and find; forsake and lose.

David then gives the plans for the temple, which he received “by the Spirit,” and a mass of gold and silver from his own treasure. He challenges the leaders: “Who then is willing to offer willingly?” They respond, and the giving is joyful. The key note is voluntary generosity. “The people rejoiced because they had given willingly.” Giving is meant to be a joy.

Then comes David’s prayer. It begins with praise: “Yours, O LORD, is the greatness and the power and the glory and the victory and the majesty, for all that is in the heavens and in the earth is yours.” It is the source of the line often used in the doxology of the Lord’s Prayer. Then comes the great humility: “Who am I, and what is my people, that we should be able to give thus willingly? For all things come from you, and of your own have we given you.” Nothing we give is ours. We hand back what was lent.

He also prays for the people’s hearts: “Keep this forever in the intentions of the thoughts of the heart of your people, and direct their hearts toward you.” David knows that the heart is the key and that only God can keep it.

The book ends with David’s death and the note that his acts are “written in the chronicles.” The great king is gone, but the work continues.
connection: Matthew 6:13 (in some manuscripts) ends the Lord’s Prayer with “For yours is the kingdom and the power and the glory forever.” 2 Corinthians 9:7: “God loves a cheerful giver.” 1 Corinthians 4:7: “What do you have that you did not receive?” Acts 20:35: “It is more blessed to give than to receive.” 2 Timothy 1:5 mentions faith passed down. Proverbs 4:23: guard your heart.
application:
Pray David’s prayer about giving: ask God to help you give willingly and joyfully.

Think about who you are charging to “know the God of your father.” Pray for them by name.

Write a letter or blessing for a younger person about what you have learned of God.
prayerPrompts: Tell God that everything you have comes from him.
Offer him something willingly and with joy.
Ask him to keep your heart loyal to him.
